title: contract-clauses-quick-checklist
content:
Personal quick checklist + redline snippets for customer contracts (scratchpad).

Purpose: fast reference when reviewing customer or partner contracts — keep short, prioritised, and pragmatic. Not a substitute for formal legal review; use as negotiation prep.

Top risks to flag quickly:
- Liability & cap: target single-digit multiples of annual fees; carve out willful misconduct/fraud. If customer insists on high cap, push for insurance or reciprocal language.
- Indemnity: narrow to third-party IP claims and direct damages; avoid broad customer indemnities for model outputs.
- Data use & ownership: explicitly state customer retains rights in their input data; vendor gets right to process for providing service and to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvement only.
- Model weights & derivatives: do NOT concede customer ownership of models, weights, or derivatives. Give customer granted rights to outputs per license, not transfer of model IP.
- Confidentiality & exceptions: tighten definition of Confidential Information and limit exceptions (e.g., compelled disclosure should require notice and narrow scope).
- Security & breach: SLA for notification timelines (48-72 hours initial, follow-up detailed report within 30 days). List basic security controls (encryption at rest, TLS in transit, SOC2). For high-risk customers, escalate to SSO/KMS requirements.
- Data retention & deletion: clear deletion triggers on termination and a deletion certificate timeline (30-90 days depending on customer size). Clarify backups and snapshot windows.
- Audit & access requests: minimize on-site audit rights; prefer remote evidence and SOC2 report exchange. For production-of-data requests, require subpoenas and customer cooperation.
- Export controls & sanctions: standard carve-ins; customer must warrant compliance for their data and users.
- Service levels & credits: be conservative on SLA metrics. Prefer reasonable best-effort with credits capped to a % of fees, not specific liquidated damages.
- Termination & transition: include transition assistance fees/time, and ensure return/destruction obligations.
- Subprocessors / subcontracting: include posting & opt-out windows for high-risk subprocessors; carve out pre-approved cloud infra partners.
- Publicity & press: require mutual consent for logos/announcements.
- Insurance: maintain commercial general liability + cyber insurance with minimum limits; get certificates on request.

Negotiation posture / quick talking points:
- "We operate a multi-tenant platform; for security we cannot transfer model weights or assign IP in the platform itself. We grant a license to use outputs for the customer's business purposes."
- "Our liability is limited to direct damages and capped at the amount paid in the prior 12 months. We can discuss higher caps for enterprise commitments with insurance backing."
- "For transparency, we will share SOC2 reports and can provide security questionnaires, but live audits must be scoped and scheduled."
- "We treat customer inputs as customer property. We will use aggregated telemetry for product improvement, but will not identify customer data in that telemetry."

Redline snippets to keep handy (copy-paste mod):
- Liability cap (vendor-first): "Except for liability resulting from vendor's willful misconduct or gross negligence, vendor's aggregate liability shall not exceed the total fees paid by customer hereunder during the 12 months preceding the claim."
- Indemnity (narrow): "Vendor will indemnify customer for third-party claims alleging that the vendor's platform infringes a third party's issued United States patents, copyrights, or trade secrets. Customer's indemnity obligations exclude claims arising from customer's data or instructions to the platform."
- Data processing: "Customer retains all right, title, and interest in Customer Data. Vendor may process Customer Data solely to provide the Services and to improve Vendor's services using aggregated, de-identified metrics. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data."
- Deletion: "Upon termination, Vendor will cease processing Customer Data and, within 30 days, delete or return Customer Data in Vendor's possession, except to the extent retention is required by law or as reasonably necessary for backup recovery; Vendor will provide certification of deletion upon request."

Notes to self during review:
- If customer requests code access or model export, escalate immediately to Legal + Applied ML: potential IP + safety risks.
- Watch for vague "use of outputs" language — prefer explicit license grant with allowed purposes.
- If customer asks for indemnity for model outputs (e.g., defamation/liability for model-made statements) push back and propose carve-outs or insurance.
- For high-reg customers (healthcare/finance), run a tailored security checklist: HITRUST/HIPAA/PCI requirements, data localization, private deployment options.

Escalation triggers (ask Legal lead):
- Reciprocal unlimited liability, open-ended indemnity, or requirement to transfer core IP.
- Unusual audit frequency or rights to source code.
- Data localization that requires infra changes or private deployments.

Practical negotiation tactics:
- Trade concessions: offer longer notice periods for termination in exchange for tighter liability limits; offer SOC2 report + penetration test summary instead of on-site audits.
- Quantify risk: convert nebulous obligations into time/cost estimates (e.g., "30 days & $X for data extraction/transition assistance").
- Keep templates: maintain a small set of fallback clauses approved by Legal for sales to use under certain thresholds.

Quick checklist (tick during first pass):
- [ ] Is liability cap present and reasonable?
- [ ] Is indemnity reciprocal or unreasonable?
- [ ] Who owns customer data? Any accidental assignment?
- [ ] Any language implying ownership of model outputs or weights?
- [ ] Audit rights scoped? Prefer SOC2 / remote evidence.
- [ ] Deletion timeline defined? Backups addressed?
- [ ] Security controls named? Any impossible customer demands?
- [ ] Subprocessor list / change notice?
- [ ] Export control and sanctions clause present?
- [ ] Termination fees / transition assistance reasonable?

Quick links to internal references I usually need:
- Confluence: Contract Standards page (linked in metadata)
- SALT: internal escalation path to Applied ML (ticket tag: AML-PRIVACY)
- Sales playbook: standard thresholds for auto-approve vs legal review (sales-quick-approvals doc)

Open questions to follow up with Legal ops:
- Default deletion certificate template?
- Standard cyber insurance minimum amounts for 2026 quotes?
- Do we have pre-approved subprocessors list to share with customers quickly?

End of scratchpad. Keep updated with any new push from Product/Applied ML about telemetry uses or new private-deploy pricing that affects negotiation points.
